messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to perform t-test on two independent samples. We have dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35] (n=10). Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36] (n=10). We need to compute t-statistic and p-value for alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01. Use two-sided test? Usually t-test for difference of means. We'll compute mean, variance, pooled variance, t-statistic, degrees of freedom (df= n1+n2-2 = 18). Then compute two-tailed p-value. Let's compute.

Dataset A: sum = 12+15+18+20+22+25+28+30+32+35 = let's sum: 12+15=27; +18=45; +20=65; +22=87; +25=112; +28=140; +30=170; +32=202; +35=237. So mean_A = 237/10 = 23.7.

Compute sum of squares: we need variance. Compute each deviation squared: (12-23.7)=-11.7 => 136.89; (15-23.7)=-8.7 => 75.69; (18-23.7)=-5.7 => 32.49; (20-23.7)=-3.7 => 13.69; (22-23.7)=-1.7 => 2.89; (25-23.7)=1.3 => 1.69; (28-23.7)=4.3 => 18.49; (30-23.7)=6.3 => 39.69; (32-23.7)=8.3 => 68.89; (35-23.7)=11.3 => 127.69. Sum of squares = let's add: 136.89+75.69=212.58; +32.49=245.07; +13.69=258.76; +2.89=261.65; +1.69=263.34; +18.49=281.83; +39.69=321.52; +68.89=390.41; +127.69=518.10. So sum of squared deviations = 518.10. Sample variance s1^2 = 518.10/(n1-1)=518.10/9=57.5667. Standard deviation s1 = sqrt(57.5667)=7.590.

Dataset B: sum = 14+17+19+21+23+26+29+31+33+36 = let's sum: 14+17=31; +19=50; +21=71; +23=94; +26=120; +29=149; +31=180; +33=213; +36=249. Mean_B = 249/10 = 24.9.

Compute deviations: (14-24.9)=-10.9 => 118.81; (17-24.9)=-7.9 => 62.41; (19-24.9)=-5.9 => 34.81; (21-24.9)=-3.9 => 15.21; (23-24.9)=-1.9 => 3.61; (26-24.9)=1.1 => 1.21; (29-24.9)=4.1 => 16.81; (31-24.9)=6.1 => 37.21; (33-24.9)=8.1 => 65.61; (36-24.9)=11.1 => 123.21. Sum of squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22; +34.81=216.03; +15.21=231.24; +3.61=234.85; +1.21=236.06; +16.81=252.87; +37.21=290.08; +65.61=355.69; +123.21=478.90. So sum of squared deviations = 478.90. Sample variance s2^2 = 478.90/9 = 53.2111. Standard deviation s2 = sqrt(53.2111)=7.295.

Now compute pooled variance: sp^2 = ((n1-1)*s1^2 + (n2-1)*s2^2)/(n1+n2-2) = (9*57.5667 + 9*53.2111)/18 = (518.1003 + 478.8999)/18 = 997.0002/18 = 55.389. Actually 997/18 = 55.3889. So sp = sqrt(55.389)=7.44.

Standard error of difference: SE = sp * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.1 + 0.1) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.2) = 7.44 * 0.4472136 = 3.327. Let's compute precisely: 7.44*0.4472136 = 3.327.

Difference in means: mean_A - mean_B = 23.7 - 24.9 = -1.2. t-statistic = (mean_A - mean_B)/SE = -1.2 / 3.327 = -0.3607. So t = -0.361 approx.

Degrees of freedom df = 18. Two-tailed p-value: For t=0.361 with df=18, p > 0.7. Let's approximate using t distribution. t=0.36, df=18. The two-tailed p-value is about 0.72. Let's compute more precisely: Using t distribution table: For df=18, t critical for alpha=0.05 two-tailed is 2.101. Our t=0.361 < 2.101, so fail to reject. For alpha=0.01, t critical is 2.878. Also fail. p-value ~ 0.72. Let's compute using python? But we can approximate. Let's compute using t distribution formula: p = 2*(1 - CDF(|t|)). For df=18, t=0.361. Using approximate: For small t, CDF ~ 0.5 + t/(sqrt(df)*sqrt(pi/2))? Not accurate. Let's approximate using online. But we can say p ≈ 0.72. Provide results: t = -0.36, df=18, p ≈ 0.72. Since p > 0.05 and > 0.01, we fail to reject null hypothesis at both significance levels. So no significant difference.

We need to use the function t_test. Provide dataset_A and dataset_B arrays. We'll call function twice: once with alpha=0.05, once with alpha=0.01. The function returns something. We need to output results. Let's call function.
